clue.text: Dish of seafood an aid to growth

parts.note: fish is the general word for seafood of the finned kind
a meal can be a dish served up, as in a meal of fish

explanation.surface: A seafood dish is said to help you grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Dish of seafood' backwards in sense: the seafood goes first, then the dish. The ground-up product is used as fertiliser and animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground dried fish is sold as a fertiliser and livestock feed, so it promotes growth in plants and animals.

clue.text: Forge raw ore in making this

definitions.text: Forge raw ore in making this

indicators.note: to forge is to hammer metal into a new shape, so these three words are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A smith hammers raw ore and produces this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: goods made by forging iron ore, and its words also hold the fodder RAW ORE IN for the anagram signalled by 'Forge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironware is household goods and tools made of iron, the very thing a forge produces from ore.

clue.text: Senior politicians will get exercise having kick around on sports ground

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes first, so the ground follows
the word for kicking is placed around the word for exercise, enclosing it

parts.note: to hoof a ball is to kick it hard
to exercise a right is to use it
Lord's is the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Top politicians are told to take exercise by kicking a ball about at a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the famous cricket ground in north London. The upper chamber of the UK Parliament has senior members, peers and bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of the British Parliament is made up of peers, many of them elder statesmen.

clue.text: Goon associated with church briefly

indicators.note: a word cut short, as in an abbreviation, signals letters lopped off the end

parts.note: ecclesial means relating to a church

explanation.surface: A clown is linked with a church, just for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles was a character in The Goon Show, a classic British radio comedy of the 1950s, whose performers and characters are called Goons. 'Eccles.' is also a standard abbreviation for things ecclesiastical.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles was one of the comic characters voiced by Spike Milligan in the British radio comedy The Goon Show.

clue.text: Prune supplied energy for run

parts.note: to prune a tree is to lop it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dried plum gave a burst of energy for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy, bounding strides.

clue.text: Douglas perhaps sober getting medical treatment

parts.note: the Douglas fir is a kind of conifer, so Douglas is an example of a fir
staid means sober, sedate and serious

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas, now on the wagon, is getting hospital care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Douglas' looks like a man's name but stands for the Douglas fir, a tree; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate medical help given to an injured or sick person before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: In favour of female academic

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone backs a woman scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is the short informal form of professor, a senior university teacher.

clue.text: Army chap trained as chemist

indicators.note: trained suggests drilling into new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier retrained to become a chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'chemist' also means the chemist's shop where medicines are dispensed, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a chemist is a shop dispensing medicines, the same as a drugstore or dispensary.

clue.text: Gaol rich crooked powerful man

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rich, corrupt tycoon ends up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small group holding power, especially a wealthy Russian magnate.

clue.text: Vegetarian food out of unopened bottles

indicators.note: bottles is a verb here: the words keep the answer contained, as a bottle holds its contents

explanation.surface: Meat-free food comes out of bottles that were never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' reads as a noun in the surface but is a verb: the words 'out of unopened' hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd pressed from soya milk, a staple protein for vegetarians.

clue.text: Veteran using net more certain to catch fish initially following change

indicators.note: the second part follows the first, coming after it

parts.note: silver is loose change, coins of silver-coloured metal

indicators.note: the word for more certain catches a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: surer means more certain

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word fish

explanation.surface: An old fisherman with his net is surer to catch fish after a change of spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' suggests fishing, but it is the internet. 'to catch' puts F, the first letter of 'fish' given by 'initially', inside SURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver surfer is a slang term for an elderly person who uses the internet, silver referring to grey hair.

clue.text: A paper surprisingly probing revolution making fresh judgement

indicators.note: something probing pushes into the word for revolution, sitting inside it

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or revolution

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so these letters are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A newspaper unexpectedly investigates a revolt and reaches a new verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests turning, but here it is an uprising; 'paper' is the word itself, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess again, so reappraising is forming a fresh assessment of something.

clue.text: Person drinking to wake up in vehicle

indicators.note: the waking word sits in the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to rouse someone is to wake them up

explanation.surface: Someone who has been drinking wakes up inside a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks heavily and merrily in company, a reveller.

clue.text: Dance with business expert after game at Twickenham

indicators.note: the expert comes after the game, as the second piece

parts.note: Twickenham is England's national rugby stadium, and RU stands for rugby union
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration, a qualified business expert

explanation.surface: A business graduate dances after a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham, in south-west London, is the home of English rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in quick time.

clue.text: Bush expels one from a spy organisation twice

indicators.note: expels means throws out, so a letter is removed
twice means the spy agency is written two times

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: George Bush throws someone out of a spy agency, and does it twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the US president linked with the CIA, but it is a plant. A plus CIA twice gives ACIACIA; 'expels' removes one I.
explanation.definitionFit: An acacia is a thorny shrub or tree of warm regions, the wattle.

clue.text: Look over section of film

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lustfully

explanation.surface: Take a look at part of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of film, and by extension one portion of a film's length.

clue.text: Arsenic's disguised in spicy spirit

indicators.note: disguised means changed in appearance, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word arsenic with its s, standing for 'arsenic is'

explanation.surface: Poison is hidden in a hot, spirited drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness is a lively, piquant or slightly risque quality, a spirited flavour.

clue.text: Was speechless, taking motorway to sea

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone driving the motorway to the coast was lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To mime is to act without words, so mimed means performed silently.

clue.text: I'm involved with venture in which leader's removed

definitions.text: I'm involved with venture in which leader's removed

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, of the word venture is taken off

explanation.surface: A sailor says he is part of an enterprise where the captain has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's removed' leaves ENTURE from 'venture'; 'involved' mixes I'M with it. The whole clue describes a rebel who ousts the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is someone who rebels against those in command, typically a sailor deposing the captain.

clue.text: Ruth to be mine before year

indicators.note: the mine comes before the year in the answer

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth will be mine in a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name but is an old word for compassion, as in 'ruthless', having none.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic noun meaning compassion or sorrow for another, surviving in ruthless.

clue.text: Speculate in article over origin

parts.note: the is the definite article
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
rise means origin, as in 'give rise to'

explanation.surface: Wondering about the beginning of things.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form theories, to speculate about how things are.

clue.text: Encouragement to have run out in vehicle

indicators.note: the cricket dismissal sits in the vehicle word

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of petrol while in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out is a cricket dismissal where a batter fails to reach the crease, scored RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an incentive or reward offered, from the carrot dangled before a donkey.

clue.text: Chamberlain perhaps to perform round Home Counties

indicators.note: the performing word goes round the region, enclosing it

parts.note: to appear on stage is to perform
the Home Counties are the counties around London, in south-east England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A court chamberlain performs on tour around the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain was the British prime minister who appeased Hitler at Munich in 1938. The Home Counties ring London in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain pursued appeasement of Nazi Germany, so he is a famous example of one who placates aggressors.

clue.text: Cloak on a small Greek goddess

parts.note: a pall is a cloak or covering, as in a pall of smoke

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess wears a little cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallas is an epithet of Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Fan to rub down athlete's essentials

to sand is to rub a surface smooth
Usain Bolt is the Jamaican sprinter, and the possessive adds the s

explanation.surface: A fan gives an athlete a rub-down, the basics of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rub down' suggests a sports massage, but it means smoothing with sandpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts and bolts are the basic practical details of something, its fundamental working parts.

clue.text: Fox catching a despicable person

indicators.note: the fox word catches the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: A fox catches a nasty character.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad is used as an insult for a loathsome, contemptible person.

clue.text: Bachelor embarrassed having produced children

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A single man blushes on becoming a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means reproduced or gave birth to offspring.

clue.text: The Thames in some parts is doubled

indicators.note: doubled means written twice, so the little word appears two times

explanation.surface: The river Thames is said to be doubled in places.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford the upper Thames is called the Isis, which is why only 'some parts' carry the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name for the stretch of the River Thames flowing through Oxford.

clue.text: Made step wildly in this

indicators.note: wildly means in a frenzied way, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Animals stepped out wildly in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a wild rush is where creatures step madly, and 'wildly' rearranges MADE STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd of animals or a crowd.

clue.text: Fashion expert perhaps does clothes symbol

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the animals dress, or surround, the symbol

a sign is a symbol

explanation.surface: A couturier dresses a symbolic figure.
